details: The United States, Japan, and South Korea conducted a rare coordinated foreign exchange intervention on July 30-31, with Japan reportedly spending approximately $528 billion to support the yen, and South Korea acting to strengthen the won. The US Treasury also participated by selling euros and buying yen. This intervention, the first of its kind for the US and Japan in 15 years, aims to stabilize markets and prevent broader risk spillovers. However, the operation raises bond-market risk for cryptocurrencies, as a rapid yen rally could trigger carry-trade unwinding and leveraged liquidations across crypto exchanges and DeFi platforms.
title: US, Japan, S. Korea Intervene to Prop Up Yen, Won

details: President Trump announced the cancellation of planned US military strikes against Iran, claiming a deal for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and progress on a nuclear program. However, Iranian officials have officially denied any such agreement, creating renewed uncertainty in the region. While oil prices initially reacted with a dip following Trump's announcement, Bitcoin's response has been minimal. These conflicting reports highlight ongoing geopolitical volatility that continues to impact energy markets and broader investor sentiment.
title: Iran Denies Trump's Hormuz Deal Amid Rising Tensions
